key_insight: An attention-fused TFT–N-BEATS model forecasts PV power across five horizons, with the abstract reporting 35–40% lower RMSE than the best baseline, TFT.
engineering_relevance: Unified forecasts from 30 minutes to 24 hours could support grid scheduling and coordinated PV–battery operation; this is forecasting research, not perovskite cell design.
method: TFT models short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes longer-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for five forecast horizons.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on multi-year DKASC datasets reports RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11, with MAPE below 5% across all datasets.
watch_item: The abstract omits RMSE units, horizon-specific results, and validation-split details, limiting assessment of operational reliability and generalization.
paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
